tasks.name: Verify opencode worktree-to-project resolution
tasks.description: FR-0.1. With an authenticated opencode, start a session inside a linked git worktree and inspect the project/project_directory/session rows in opencode.db (read-only). Determine whether the worktree gets its own project row or resolves to the parent repository. Record the finding in the spec. If it resolves to the parent, the correlation design in phase-2 must be revised before implementation. BLOCKING for phase-2.

tasks.name: Verify permission.ask behaviour under --auto
tasks.description: FR-0.2. Determine whether the permission.ask plugin hook still fires when opencode is launched with --auto. Record whether bypass and Sebenza-side gating can coexist or are mutually exclusive. BLOCKING for phase-3 wiring. [OUTCOME 2026-07-28: partially resolved. --auto bypasses permission.ask; the hook is config-ruleset-gated, not per-tool-call; an `ask` rule hangs non-interactive `run`. Findings in spec.md FR-0.2. Residual question - can permission.ask fire and be honoured at all - moved to phase-3-task-1 as a hard gate.]

tasks.name: Capture an opencode export fixture
tasks.description: FR-0.3. Commit a real `opencode export <id>` JSON payload as testdata/. This is the basis for all history parser tests and cannot be invented from documentation. Requires an authenticated opencode.

tasks.name: Investigate unconditional claude_conversation_service dispatch
tasks.description: FR-0.4. server.rs:1382 (interrupt) and ~1522 (streaming WebSocket) call claude_conversation_service::read_worktree_conversation with no agent match, unlike the paths that branch. Determine empirically whether codex interrupt/streaming is broken today despite declaring interrupt: true. Fix it or document the limitation and correct the capability. Must be resolved before any dispatch generalisation, or the defect quadruples.

tasks.name: Write tests for loopback-default bind
tasks.description: FR-0.5. Failing tests asserting the server binds 127.0.0.1 by default and binds all interfaces only when the explicit opt-in flag/env is set.

tasks.name: Implement loopback-default bind with explicit LAN opt-in
tasks.description: FR-0.5. Change main.rs:82 from SocketAddr::from(([0,0,0,0], port)) to loopback by default, adding an explicit flag/env to opt into all interfaces. Behaviour change for anyone reaching the dashboard from another machine - must be called out in release notes. Unblocks the permission routes in phase-3.

tasks.name: Phase verification & checkpoint
tasks.description: Per workflow.md: ensure test coverage for phase changes, run cargo test and CI=true npm test, propose manual verification, await confirmation, attach git-notes verification report, record checkpoint_sha.

tasks.name: Write tests for BuiltinAgentId enum and per-agent invocation split
tasks.description: FR-1.1. Failing tests covering the enum-based registry and the extraction of built_in_invocation's if/else into per-agent functions, preserving existing claude and codex argv exactly (fresh, resume, fork, yolo, system prompt, prompt suffix).

tasks.name: Introduce BuiltinAgentId and refactor invocation building
tasks.description: FR-1.1. Replace AgentImplementation::Builtin(String) with Builtin(BuiltinAgentId) for Claude and Codex only. Split built_in_invocation (agent_service.rs:74-132) into named per-agent functions dispatched by enum match. No new agents in this task - this is the seam that Opencode plugs into in phase-2, and that a future goose track reuses.

tasks.name: Write tests for new capability fields and wire contract
tasks.description: FR-1.3. Failing tests for fork, pinnable_session_id and permission_interception on AgentCapabilities and AgentCapabilitiesWire, including explicit false for custom agents so schema parse does not break.

tasks.name: Add capability fields and widen Zod schemas
tasks.description: FR-1.3, FR-6.3. Add the three fields to both Rust structs and to AgentCapabilitiesSchema. Widen BuiltInAgentIdSchema (schemas.ts:22), AutoNameProviderSchema (217) and WorktreeConversationProviderSchema (289 plus literals at 292, 300). permission_interception is wire-visible.

tasks.name: Write tests for unified builtin registry
tasks.description: FR-1.2. Failing tests asserting config_view.rs's agent summaries derive from agent_registry.rs - one builtin list, one capability struct - and that build_app_config exposes the same agents and capabilities as list_agent_details.

tasks.name: Unify the duplicate builtin agent registries
tasks.description: FR-1.2. config_view.rs:25-48 currently defines its own builtin_agent_summaries(), its own AgentCapabilities struct and its own shadow filter, and server.rs:366 serves it as build_app_config - which is what populates config.agents and therefore the Create Worktree picker. Derive it from agent_registry.rs so new agents and capabilities cannot silently drift between the two.

tasks.name: Write tests for registry-resolved server dispatch
tasks.description: FR-1.5. Failing tests asserting refresh_agent_terminal, agents_conversation, prepare_agent_send and submit_delay_for_branch resolve the agent via get_agent_definition and match on BuiltinAgentId rather than on raw strings.

tasks.name: Route all server dispatch sites through the registry
tasks.description: FR-1.5. Replace the Some("claude")/Some("codex") string matches at server.rs 1162-63, 1233-34, 1283-84 with a resolve-then-enum-match, following the pattern submit_delay_for_branch (919-933) already uses. Add StreamProvider plumbing in agent_stream.rs. Widening string arms instead would forfeit the exhaustiveness guarantee this refactor exists for.

tasks.name: Write tests for capability-driven frontend gating
tasks.description: FR-6.2, FR-6.4. Failing tests for canFork reading capabilities.fork, supportsWorktreeChat failing closed rather than falling back to a hardcoded id list, WorktreeConversationPanel's label and chat gate, MobileChatSurface provider dispatch, and capability-derived 409 message text.

tasks.name: Replace hardcoded agent identity in the frontend and API messages
tasks.description: FR-6.2, FR-6.4. App.tsx:230 canFork to capability; App.tsx:162-169 supportsWorktreeChat fallback to false (fail closed, hide the tab); WorktreeConversationPanel.tsx:169-170 label and supportsAgentChat; MobileChatSurface.tsx:90,321. Replace the 'only available for Claude and Codex worktrees' 409 strings with text derived from declared capabilities.

tasks.name: Phase verification & checkpoint
tasks.description: Per workflow.md. Behaviour for claude and codex must be unchanged end-to-end - this phase is a pure refactor with no new agents.

phases.name: opencode at full parity (+ shared controls)

tasks.name: Write tests for opencode invocation and binary resolution
tasks.description: FR-3.2, FR-3.7. Failing tests for fresh/-c/-s/--fork argv, --auto appended like the other flag-based bypasses, --title/--agent/--model/--dir, and binary resolution that probes ~/.opencode/bin explicitly since a plain which() can fail on a working install.

tasks.name: Implement the Opencode variant, invocations and binary probe
tasks.description: FR-3.1, FR-3.2, FR-3.7. Add Opencode to BuiltinAgentId as its own exhaustiveness sweep and handle every resulting error. Implement invocations and the ~/.opencode/bin-aware resolution.

tasks.name: Write tests for the opencode plugin shim
tasks.description: FR-3.3, FR-3.4, FR-5.6. Failing tests asserting the generated .opencode/plugins/sebenza.js imports nothing, embeds no branch/worktree/profile literals (per-worktree data arrives via SEBENZA_* env vars), is byte-stable across worktrees, is written as a full overwrite, and maps the event hook correctly.

tasks.name: Generate the opencode plugin shim and extend agentctl
tasks.description: FR-3.3, FR-3.4. Emit an import-free JS shim using only runtime globals. Map the generic event hook: EventSessionCreated to session-id capture (no polling), EventSessionIdle to idle, EventSessionError to runtime error, tool.execute.before to running, tool.execute.after to PR detection via the existing maybe_send_pr_opened. Add opencode-* agentctl subcommands; all decision logic stays in the Python helper, never reimplemented in JS. This is the first generated-JS artifact in the codebase.

tasks.name: Write tests for opencode history via the CLI
tasks.description: FR-3.5. Failing tests against the phase-0 export fixture, asserting history is read via `opencode session list` and `opencode export <id> --sanitize`, that opencode.db is never opened, and that unknown fields in the export JSON are tolerated.

tasks.name: Implement opencode session discovery and conversation service
tasks.description: FR-3.5. Add adapters/opencode_session_log.rs shelling out to session list and export --sanitize, plus services/opencode_conversation_service.rs emitting AgentsUiMessage. --sanitize gives upstream-defined secret redaction, preferable to anything Sebenza would implement itself. Add the Opencode variant to DiscoverableAgentKind and WorktreeConversationProvider.

tasks.name: Implement worktree-to-session correlation per the phase-0 finding
tasks.description: FR-3.6. Correlate via project.worktree to session directory/path as established by phase-0-task-1. If that task found opencode resolves a linked worktree to the parent repository, implement the revised approach it recommends instead - do not assume per-worktree partitioning.

tasks.name: Write tests for artifact git-exclusion and env file permissions
tasks.description: FR-5.1, FR-5.5. Failing tests asserting all generated in-worktree artifacts are added to info/exclude (.opencode/plugins/, and retroactively .claude/settings.local.json), and that control.env and runtime.env are written 0600.

tasks.name: Git-exclude generated artifacts and harden env file modes
tasks.description: FR-5.1, FR-5.5. Generalise ensure_generated_codex_hooks_ignored from a single constant to a path list, so any future agent's artifact is covered by construction. Apply set_mode_600 in write_control_env and write_runtime_env - runtime.env merges .env.local project secrets, so the exposure is wider than the control token alone.

tasks.name: Write tests for untrusted-plugin scan and per-repo confirmation
tasks.description: FR-5.2, FR-5.3. SHARED CONTROL. Failing tests for: detecting plugin files Sebenza did not write by comparing against a stored hash of bytes last written (not a recomputed expectation); the store living outside the worktree in <git-common-dir>/.ai/sebenza/; auto-launch blocked pending confirmation; the decision remembered per repository; and the store being unwritable from the worktree.

tasks.name: Implement untrusted-plugin scan, confirmation store and audit events
tasks.description: FR-5.2 to FR-5.4, FR-5.8. Scan before launch, block, and require per-repo confirmation stored at control-token trust tier outside the worktree. Offer opencode's --pure (runs without external plugins) as the safe terminal-only fallback when the user declines. Persist audit events (agent_launched with bypass mode, artifact_written/overwritten with mismatch boolean, untrusted_plugin_detected) under <git-common-dir>/.ai/sebenza/, carrying no secrets. Keep the scan's plugin-path set data-driven so a future agent is a config change, not a code change.

tasks.name: Write tests for docker mounts and PATH fallback
tasks.description: FR-6.1. Failing pure-function assertions on build_docker_run_args output, following docker.rs's existing test module pattern - no Docker daemon required.

tasks.name: Add docker config and session-data mounts
tasks.description: FR-6.1. Bind-mount ~/.config/opencode and ~/.local/share/opencode unconditionally, matching the existing claude/codex mounts, so history parity holds on host and docker. Add /root/.opencode/bin to DOCKER_PATH_FALLBACK. Without the config mount a containerised run has no provider credentials at all.

tasks.name: Implement shadow resolution and the durable override notice
tasks.description: FR-1.6. Builtin wins over a shadowed custom-agent id, emitting a durable shadowed_custom_agent_detected event that names the id and states the key-rename escape hatch. Remove ONLY the opencode entry from .ai/sebenza.example.yaml - goose is NOT becoming builtin in this track, so its custom-agent entry must remain and keep working. Add a compatibility test that loads the pre-change example config. Breaking change for existing users; must never fail silently.

tasks.name: Add opencode to auto-naming, init analysis and version reporting
tasks.description: FR-3.8, FR-6.5, FR-6.6. Add the opencode arm to llm_spawn.rs::build_llm_args (opencode run --format json) and to init_authoring.rs (InitAgent, authoring_agent(), build_init_agent_command()) - a separate fifth dispatch axis. Add the AutoNameProvider variant plus its YAML-parsing counterpart at config.rs:273-274. Act on init.rs:52's existing opencode probe, report the detected version, document the minimum supported version in tech-stack.md, and update README prerequisites.

tasks.name: Phase verification & checkpoint
tasks.description: Per workflow.md. Manual verification must cover creating an opencode worktree, driving it via terminal and chat, history under both host and docker runtimes, status transitions, resume and fork, the untrusted-plugin confirmation path including the --pure decline fallback, and confirming no generated artifact appears in git status.

tasks.name: Spike: verify permission.ask can fire and be honoured
tasks.description: Residue of phase-0-task-2, which established that --auto bypasses permission.ask, that permission.ask is config-ruleset-gated rather than per-tool-call, and that `permission: {bash: "ask"}` hangs non-interactive `opencode run`. What remains unproven is whether permission.ask fires AT ALL and whether mutating output.status is honoured. Build a harness matching how Sebenza actually launches agents - an interactive TUI in a tmux pane - and/or `opencode serve` + a scripted client. Set a project permission rule evaluating to `ask`, install a probe plugin that logs the call and sets status, and confirm the tool is allowed or denied accordingly. HARD GATE: if permission.ask cannot be driven this way, the remaining phase-3 tasks are not buildable as designed and the phase must be redesigned or descoped. Do not begin phase-3-task-2 until this resolves.

tasks.name: Write tests for the asymmetric credential model
tasks.description: FR-4.2. Failing tests asserting the resolve route REJECTS a verdict presented with only the control token; that it requires a per-request resolver secret minted server-side; that the secret never appears in control.env, runtime.env or any worktree-readable file; and that a verdict is single-use and bound to session plus request id. This closes the flaw where the gated process, which holds SEBENZA_CONTROL_TOKEN, could approve its own request.

tasks.name: Implement the pending-decision store and resolver secrets
tasks.description: FR-4.2, FR-4.3. Mirror agent_stream.rs's AgentStreamManager/RunState idiom: a concurrent map of request ids to oneshot senders resolved by a side-channel call. In-memory, not durable across restart. Mint per-request resolver secrets delivered only via the WS push payload and the CLI response.

tasks.name: Write tests for submit/resolve routes, fail-closed paths and the cap
tasks.description: FR-4.4 to FR-4.8, FR-4.11. Failing tests for: the submit handler awaiting a oneshot receiver with no lock held across the await; timeout, HTTP error and connection reset all resolving to deny; the server timeout being authoritative; the per-session and global pending cap with auto-deny beyond it; timeout enforcement independent of WS delivery; and both routes bound to loopback.

tasks.name: Implement the submit and resolve routes
tasks.description: FR-4.4 to FR-4.8, FR-4.11, FR-5.8. Loopback-bound routes with the asymmetric auth model, fail-closed on every failure mode, server-authoritative timeout, pending cap with auto-deny, and the permission_decision (including resolution source) and pending_permission_cap_hit audit events. Never block the async runtime.

tasks.name: Write tests for the shim permission.ask round-trip
tasks.description: FR-4.1, FR-4.5. Failing tests asserting the shim calls permission.ask, awaits a verdict via fetch (a runtime global under opencode's bundled Bun, so the import-free constraint from phase-2 still holds), writes it into output.status, and fails closed on timeout or error.

tasks.name: Implement permission.ask in the generated shim
tasks.description: FR-4.1. Extend the phase-2 shim to submit the request, await the verdict, and set output.status. Apply the phase-0-task-2 finding: if permission.ask does not fire under --auto, the two features are mutually exclusive and the UI must prevent enabling both.

tasks.name: Implement the dashboard permission prompt and WS push
tasks.description: FR-4.9. Push pending requests over the existing WS event stream carrying the resolver secret, and render a prompt card modelled on AskUserQuestionCard's look - its plumbing is transcript-level with no backend counterpart and is not reusable.

tasks.name: Implement CLI parity for pending permission requests
tasks.description: FR-4.9. sebenza-cli commands to list and answer pending requests, per Guiding Principle 8. This is also the designed fallback when a WS push is missed.

tasks.name: Implement per-profile timeout and visible timeout denial
tasks.description: FR-4.6, FR-4.10. Add a configurable per-profile decision timeout. A timeout-caused denial must be visible in the transcript and worktree status so a stalled worktree reads as 'waited for you, then denied' rather than as a hung agent.

tasks.name: Phase verification & checkpoint
tasks.description: Per workflow.md. Manual verification must cover: approving a tool call, denying one, letting one time out and confirming the denial is visible, and confirming the resolve route rejects a control-token-only verdict.
